core/validate.py - post-parse reconciliation.

The zero-data guard in the UI only catches ``entities == 0``. A recipe can also
match the WRONG rows and produce a plausible-but-wrong result, which is more
dangerous than a blank export because nothing looks broken. Example seen on a real
LPP PO (PO_637JO_2627182):

    correct  -> 24 detail rows  "…MEN`S TROUSERS 80X BEIGE PCS 744 10.20 7,588.80"  total 9000
    wrong #1 -> 16 pack rows    "637JO-80X-T01 PACK 2 186 372"                       total   32
    wrong #2 -> 10 bare rows    "637JO-80X-S PCS 372"                                total 4230

Both wrong variants share a tell-tale signature: no unit price was captured, and/or
only a small fraction of the unit-bearing lines got matched. ``reconcile`` turns
those signals into human-readable warnings. Per product decision the caller WARNS
but still exports -- the operator makes the final call.
One colour/size quantity that disagrees with the PDF's printed subtotal.

Cross-check parsed colour/size quantities against the PDF's printed subtotals.

    Runs for EVERY parse (cached or not). Two independent checks, each gated by a
    recipe flag the AI set at synthesis time:

      * ``has_color_total`` -> for each colour the summed line quantities must equal
        the summed printed ROW TOTALs of that colour's lines (the matrix ROW TOTAL
        column; for matrix_2axis this aggregates the inseam rows of one colour).
      * ``has_size_total`` -> for each size the summed line quantities must equal the
        printed bottom TOTAL row of that size. A sanity guard drops a captured TOTAL
        row whose own sum does not match the entity's parsed total, so a mis-assigned
        global/per-colour restatement can never raise a false alarm.

    Returns ``[]`` when there is nothing printed to check against (e.g. line_items,
    whose PDFs print only a block GRAND TOTAL), so the function is always safe to
    call. Per-row internal consistency (every line's parsed sum == its printed row
    total) is covered by the per-colour check when a layout prints one row per
    colour; for multi-inseam colours the per-colour aggregation is what is checked.
件 与 PDF 行小计
件 与 PDF 小计

Cross-check each entity's parsed grand total / amount against the PDF's
    printed figures (structural parsers capture them into ``printed_total_qty`` /
    ``printed_total_amount``). Returns a list of hard-block messages (empty == ok).

    * total gate: parsed ``entity.total_qty`` must equal the printed quantity
      (allowing the European-thousands 1000x ambiguity via ``thousands_match``).
    * amount gate: ``sum(qty * unit_price)`` must equal the printed amount within
      a 1% / $1 band (catches a wrong unit-price column read even when the
      quantity total happens to be right).
Return a list of human-readable warnings (empty == looks consistent).
